title: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
description: Introduction to the core concepts of OOP in Java.
notes: OOP is a programming paradigm based on the concept of 'objects', which can contain data and code. The four pillars are Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, and Abstraction.
examples: Example: A 'Car' object with properties like 'color' and 'model', and methods like 'drive()'.
codeSnippets: public class Car { String color; void drive() { System.out.println("Driving..."); } }
interviewQuestions: What are the main pillars of OOP?
Why use OOP over procedural programming?
practiceQuestions: Create a class and instantiate an object of it.
Implement a class with multiple attributes and methods.

title: Classes & Objects
description: Understanding the blueprint and the instance.
notes: A class is a blueprint for creating objects. An object is an instance of a class.
codeSnippets: class Student { String name; int age; } Student s1 = new Student();
interviewQuestions: Difference between a class and an object?
What is the 'new' keyword in Java?
practiceQuestions: Define a class 'Book' with attributes title, author, and price.

title: Inheritance
description: Mechanism where one class acquires properties of another.
notes: Inheritance allows a subclass to inherit fields and methods from a superclass using the 'extends' keyword.
codeSnippets: class Animal { void eat() {} } class Dog extends Animal { void bark() {} }
practiceQuestions: Implement a hierarchy: Vehicle -> Car -> ElectricCar.

title: Polymorphism
description: Ability of a message to be displayed in more than one form.
codeSnippets: class Calc { int add(int a, int b) { return a+b; } int add(int a, int b, int c) { return a+b+c; } }
practiceQuestions: Create a class with overloaded methods for calculating area of different shapes.

title: Abstraction
description: Hiding internal details and showing only functionality.
notes: Achieved via abstract classes and interfaces.
codeSnippets: abstract class Shape { abstract void draw(); } class Circle extends Shape { void draw() { System.out.println("Circle"); } }
practiceQuestions: Design an abstract class 'Employee' with an abstract method 'calculateSalary()'.

title: Encapsulation
description: Wrapping data and methods into a single unit.
notes: Use private variables and public getter/setter methods.
examples: Private field 'balance' in 'Account' class with getBalance() and setBalance().
codeSnippets: class Account { private double balance; public double getBalance() { return balance; } }
interviewQuestions: What is the benefit of encapsulation?
How do you achieve encapsulation in Java?
practiceQuestions: Create a 'Person' class with private fields and public getters/setters.

title: Collections
description: Framework to store and manipulate group of objects.
examples: ArrayList for dynamic arrays, HashMap for key-value pairs.
practiceQuestions: Implement a program to count occurrences of each word in a string using HashMap.

title: Exception Handling
notes: Try-catch-finally blocks, throw, and throws keywords.
examples: Handling ArithmeticException during division by zero.
codeSnippets: try { int x = 10/0; } catch (Exception e) { System.out.println(e); }
interviewQuestions: What is the purpose of the 'finally' block?
practiceQuestions: Write a program to handle multiple exceptions using a single catch block.

title: Multithreading
description: Concurrent execution of two or more parts of a program.
notes: Thread class, Runnable interface, lifecycle of a thread.
examples: Running two threads for printing 'Hello' and 'World' simultaneously.
codeSnippets: class MyThread extends Thread { public void run() { System.out.println("Run"); } }
interviewQuestions: What is the 'join()' method in Thread class?
practiceQuestions: Implement a producer-consumer problem using multithreading.

title: Streams API
description: Sequence of elements supporting sequential and parallel aggregate operations.
examples: Filtering a list of integers to get only even numbers.
practiceQuestions: Use Streams to find the sum of squares of all even numbers in a list.

title: Generics
description: Allows classes and methods to operate on objects of various types.
notes: Type safety, Generic classes and methods.
examples: Generic class 'Box<T>' that can hold any object type.
codeSnippets: class Box<T> { T value; public void set(T val) { this.value = val; } }
practiceQuestions: Create a generic method to swap two elements in an array.

title: Lambda Expressions
description: A short way to represent a functional interface.
examples: Implementing a simple addition using lambda.
interviewQuestions: Relationship between Lambdas and Anonymous Inner Classes?
practiceQuestions: Implement a custom functional interface and use it with a lambda expression.

title: Reflection API
description: Ability to examine or modify the runtime behavior of applications.
examples: Getting all methods of a class at runtime.
codeSnippets: Class<?> clazz = String.class; Method[] methods = clazz.getDeclaredMethods();
interviewQuestions: What is the use of the Reflection API?
practiceQuestions: Write a program to call a private method of a class using Reflection.

title: Synchronization
description: Controlling access of multiple threads to a shared resource.
examples: A shared counter incremented by multiple threads.
practiceQuestions: Create a thread-safe Singleton class in Java.
